correctness.rationale: Conditional Bernoulli cumulant generating functions yield the exact two third-cumulant integrals. The cubic identity makes the all-time strict gap positive. The zero-/one-flip Poisson expansion establishes opposite short-time coefficients. A bounded-jump martingale CLT with fourth-moment uniform integrability yields the common positive Gaussian limit; direct integration evaluates its coefficient. The package contains a separate Poisson-beta and Bessel-propagator numerical cross-check passing 97 comparisons; experiments are only corroborative.

originality.rationale: The 2020 general current paper, 2023 four-disorder paper and 2024 follow-up were compared by implication. They supply cumulant generating functions and all ingredients but state variance and full-distribution results, not the evaluated all-time strict third-cumulant ordering with opposite short-time signs and the analytical long-time coefficient. The 2023 source expressly proposes higher cumulants as further research. General generating functions imply computability but do not themselves establish the evaluated sign reversal; this is a risk recorded below.
residual_risks: The parent complete generating function determines the third cumulant implicitly, so further published differentiation or general skewness theorems could supersede the evaluated sign conclusion.

value.rationale: The parent paper explicitly motivates higher-current-cumulant analysis. The new strict all-time third-order preparation-ordering theorem, rigorous sign reversal only under dual quenching, and exact contrasting small-time/common long-time constants expose a change in transport asymmetry not present in the variance. It is a natural global comparison of two experimentally motivated preparations, not a contrived parameter specialization.
